note: Review performed against the North Star and the blocker register. The register item `corruption-document` is claimed FIXED in this draft's own changelog but is demonstrably still present — I flag it explicitly as unresolved, then spend the rest of the review on new failure modes, pressing the competitor/PM angle as directed.

findings.criterion: All — an unreadable plan cannot certify any criterion
findings.message: This is the register item, STILL UNRESOLVED — and worse, the draft now asserts it is fixed while the artifact refutes the assertion on its face. The "Round-3 re-emission, deduplicated" contains: (a) raw search/replace conflict markers (`>>>>`, `<<<<`, `====`) in the body; (b) THREE copies of the North Star; (c) a full second copy of the master plan embedded mid-sentence inside launch-surface item 2 — the exact defect the changelog claims was "excised"; (d) the double phase numbering ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 —", "Phase 4 — Phase 3 —") the changelog claims was collapsed, including TWO distinct sections titled "Phase 4"; (e) a third full copy embedded inside changelog item 1, which recursively contains the corrupted round-2 artifact again. Consequence: Phases 4 (pricing), 5 (surfaces), and 6–7 exist ONLY inside embedded corrupted copies — the outer "clean" document terminates mid-Phase-3, so the canonical text serving criteria 2, 5, and 6 is not recoverable from a single authoritative sequence. Separately from readability, a changelog that reports "Corruption — FIXED" over an artifact that still contains it is itself an honesty defect in a plan whose entire theme is honest provenance. Not lockable in this state.

findings.criterion: 1 (swarm spend visible going forward) and 4 (history recovered)
findings.message: The single-owner matrix is presented as closed but has an unowned class: sessions that go TERMINAL between the Phase-0 snapshot and the Phase-3 deploy. Walk it: (a) they are not in the snapshot, so the Phase-6 backfill — which "reads the frozen snapshot exclusively" — reports them no-sidecar; (b) they HAVE registry rows, so the orphan-sidecar sweep ("no registry row") skips them; (c) they never had a finalize attempt under the new substrate, so there is no `finalize-deferred` record for the sweep to retry; (d) they are already terminal at deploy, so no reconcile-dead TRANSITION ever fires for them. Phase 6's deferral explicitly refuses a second backfill mode against the live root, claiming the orphan sweep covers post-snapshot dirs — false for registered sessions. The bitter irony a competitor would seize on: this population is guaranteed to be LARGE, because it is this effort's own multi-week Crucible/Foreman build, which spawns exactly the swarm sessions criterion 1 exists to measure. The plan's flagship population re-enacts the intake failure (registered, terminal, forever unmeasured) during its own construction. Fix direction: the sweep must also own "terminal registry session with NO usage record," reading the live sidecar root, not only `finalize-deferred` retries.

findings.topic: sweep-vs-backfill owner overlap on archived deferrals
findings.section: Phase 1 repair path · Phase 3 terminality rule · Phase 0 exclusivity claim
findings.criterion: 3 (a later live finalize can still measure) and 4
findings.message: Three internal inconsistencies interlock around the deferred→archive path. First, the terminality rule has the sweep check whether a sidecar exists "in the live root and the Phase-0 archive" — so the sweep READS the archive, directly contradicting Phase 0's "the Phase 6 backfill tool points at this snapshot exclusively." Second, for a deferred record whose sidecar exists only in the archive, the sweep can see it but (per archive exclusivity) may not measure from it, and exhaustion never fires (sidecar not absent) — producing a by-design infinite retry loop every ~30 minutes for weeks until Phase 6, with two owners (sweep per the matrix, backfill per Phase 1's repair text) both claiming the same records. Third, Phase 1 promises "the Phase 6 backfill measures them [the 3 repaired sessions] through the normal claim path" without establishing that those sessions' sidecars exist in the archive at all — they were stamped `sidecar-root-unavailable`, i.e., the one population for which sidecar presence is precisely NOT evidenced. If absent from both roots, the terminality rule exhausts them to terminal `unmeasured` within ~10h of the Phase-3 deploy — weeks before Phase 6 — and the repair script's single-run latch forbids the only sanctioned resurrection path from running again. The plan must state which owner measures archive-only deferrals, and must condition the Phase-1 promise on verified archive presence.

findings.topic: provenance conflation of forward sweep with historical backfill
findings.section: Phase 3 orphan-sidecar sweep + unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through · Phase 2 closed vocabulary
findings.message: `measured-backfill` was locked (decision 2) as the provenance of the ONE-SHOT historical recovery — that is what makes it "auditable forever." The plan then reuses the identical label for two permanently-ongoing forward mechanisms: orphan-sidecar sweep captures and unwrapped shared-cwd child records. After Phase 6, an auditor can no longer answer "was this record recovered by the audited historical backfill run, or minted last Tuesday by the sweep?" — the audit distinction decision 2 exists to preserve is destroyed by construction, and the CLOSED usage_state vocabulary (frozen in Phase 2) contains no `measured-swept`/`measured-late` value to fix it without a plan amendment. A competitor's telemetry product keeps ingestion-path provenance distinct as table stakes. Compounding this: since eager in-process finalize for agy-dispatch is explicitly deferred, the 106-of-111 swarm population — the stated reason criterion 1 exists — will land predominantly under this conflated label, meaning the headline deliverable ships with its provenance story blurred. Add a distinct forward-sweep provenance value to the closed vocabulary now, while it is still amendable at plan time.

findings.section: Phase 5 surfaces (dashboard + project window rollup lines)
findings.criterion: 2 (interactive spend renders on the dashboard and project window)
findings.message: The plan adds per-session spend aggregation (`measured_sessions`, general lines, usage_state distribution, "N measured of M") to the dashboard and project-window renders, backed by per-session cost files under `.anchor/run-costs/` — but says nothing about render-path cost. This codebase has a documented, dated incident of exactly this failure: the 2026-06-16 perf fix exists because a per-render full scan of a growing record directory pushed `GET /` past the health check's 5s timeout once the population hit ~1k, and the fix mandated targeted per-id lookups, never `list_records()`. The run-cost population starts at 111+ and grows monotonically with every swarm launch (plus synthetic `sidecar:<uuid>` child rows). A competitor plan — or this repo's own prior art — would specify the aggregation as cached/incremental (e.g., computed at finalize time and folded into the existing cached rollup) rather than scan-at-render. Absent that specification, Phase 5 is on rails to reintroduce the red-banner regression the CLAUDE.md perf note memorializes.

findings.topic: native engine usage emission ignored for wired spawners
findings.section: Phase 2 evidence layer · Phase 3 launch-surface table
findings.message: Competitor press: the engine already emits authoritative usage at the source — the stream-json result envelope carries usage/cost (the plan's own `job_runner` row keeps envelope measurement for exactly this reason), and Claude Code supports telemetry export. Yet for the other WIRED non-interactive spawners (Gandalf shard jobs, summarizer runner calls — all stream-json paths through `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD`), the plan routes measurement through the sidecar-scraping stack: mtime-quiesce heuristics, a parser version fence, and a race against engine retention pruning. A competitor meters push-at-source where the source offers it and reserves file scraping for the paths that truly need it (interactive PTY sessions, unwrapped orphans, backfill). The plan never evaluates this split; adopting envelope-first for envelope-capable spawners would shrink the fragile surface the parser fence exists to defend. Refinement, not relitigation — the sidecar substrate remains necessary for the interactive and historical paths the North Star names.

findings.section: Phase 3 unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through · Phase 5 honest counting / coverage report
findings.message: The unwrapped-sub-agent mechanism mints records whose `session_id` (`sidecar:<engine-uuid>`) corresponds to no registry session, while every counting surface is defined over registry sessions: honest counting renders "N measured of M total" with M = registry population, and the coverage report reports "the fraction of registry sessions measured." Child records therefore contribute tokens to effort/fleet sums but exist outside both the numerator-denominator contract and the coverage ratio — a reader can observe rollup token totals that exceed what the "N measured of M" sessions could account for, with no surface explaining the residue. Specify whether child rows count as sessions (and in which denominator) or are rendered as an explicit separate line (e.g., "+K unattributed sub-agent records"), so the honest-counting invariant stays literally checkable.
